mt: 'IN2WRITING WORKSHOP' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE SERIES BY ITS THIRD AND FOURTH EDITIONS, TWO OF THEM AT CHI THAT THE CENSUS DOES NOT HAVE; THE FIRST WORKSHOP AND ITS READER STUDY NOT CARRIED; NO EDITOR NAMED
d: THE SERIES, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The In2Writing workshop is an academic event focused on Intelligent and Interactive Writing Assistants.' Overview: name; purpose ('To facilitate interdisciplinary discussions around writing assistants, human-AI co-writing, education risks, and the future of writing tools'); past events ('In2Writing 2024 (Third Workshop): Held in Honolulu in May 2024 (proceedings published by ACM)'; the Fourth, Albuquerque, May 2025, with NAACL, '11 papers'); the official website. Six cards: GitHub, ACM Digital Library, ACL Anthology (two), OpenReview, acm sigchi.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the workshop, the Overview names it, states its purpose and gives its two most recent editions and its website.
findings: TWO EDITIONS THE CENSUS DOES NOT HAVE. 'In2Writing 2024 (Third Workshop): Held in Honolulu in May 2024 (proceedings published by ACM).' The acm sigchi card: 'We will build off the successful workshop at CHI23 (The Second In2Writing Workshop)'. The ACL Anthology venue page the census saved lists two volumes, 2022 ('15 papers') and 2025 ('11 papers'), and the census row's record object counts only the first and the fourth. The second and third workshops, held at CHI and published by ACM, are outside the census row.

THE FOURTH AT ITS GRAIN. '11 papers' and the place and partner agree with the 2025 volume ('Month: May Year: 2025 Address: Albuquerque, New Mexico, US'). 'AI writing assistants in universities' answers the volume's Tanzania survey ('a structured survey of 1,005 university students'). The 2025 paper the census row reads for authorship, 'Interaction-Required Suggestions for Control, Ownership, and Awareness in Human- AI Co-Writing', is not named.

THE FIRST WORKSHOP NOT CARRIED. The composition does not mention 2022. The census row's reading rests on that volume's reader study: 'Participants’ task was to decide whether a continuation was written with an AI-tool or not', with 'low accuracy for differentiating between text types' and overconfidence. The series' founding year, its Dublin meeting and that study are absent.

NO EDITOR NAMED. The census names seven editors per volume ('Ting-Hao 'Kenneth' Huang , Vipul Raheja , Dongyeop Kang ...'; 'Vishakh Padmakumar , Katy Gero ...') and the ACL as publisher. The composition names ACM for the third volume and NAACL as the fourth's host, and no person. Its official website is a GitHub page; the census row's address is the ACL Anthology venue, whose identifier the composition carries only on a card ('Acronym: In2Writing; Venue ID: in2writing').
analysis: The series composed by its latest editions, two of them at CHI and absent from the census row. The first workshop, whose reader study is the census row's reason for holding the series, and every editor are absent.
per_note: ACM and NAACL named, no editor; the venue ID on an ACL Anthology card; proceedings carded.
